evidence.quote: Let $S$ be a positive definite matrix on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $U$ be a proper lower semicontinuous convex function, possibly taking the value $+\infty$.

outputs.exact_statement: There is an absolute constant $C<\infty$ with the following property. For every $n\ge1$, every centered log-concave probability measure $\mu$ with a Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^n$, and every $a>0$ satisfying [eq:intro-subgaussian] for $X\sim\mu$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\mu(f^2)\le C a^2\int_{\mathbb R^n}|Df|^2\,d\mu \qquad\text{for every }f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n).$$ The same constant works in every dimension.
Under the assumptions of Theorem 1, every $ u\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^n)$ satisfies $$W_2( u,\mu)^2\le Ca^2 H( u\mid\mu),$$ with the same absolute constant $C$ as in that theorem.

Let $S$ be a positive definite matrix on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $U$ be a proper lower semicontinuous convex function, possibly taking the value $+\infty$. Suppose $$d\pi(x)=Z^{-1}\exp\{-\tfrac12\langle x,Sx\rangle-U(x)\}\,dx$$ is a probability with a full dimensional support. Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}_\pi(f^2)\le2\mathbb E_\pi\langle Df,S^{-1}Df\rangle,
 \qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_\pi(f)\le\mathbb E_\pi\langle Df,S^{-1}Df\rangle.$$ The inequalities hold first for compact smooth tests, and then for functions obtained by finite-energy approximation.

 1\le R_s\le1+s.$$

Let $\mu$ satisfy Equation [eq:critical-normalization], with $a\le1$. Fix a compact interval $J\subset(0,1/2)$. There is a constant $C_J$, independent of the dimension and of the support radius of $\mu$, with the following property. For $s\in J$, put $\lambda=R_s^{-1}$. If $\sigma$ is any probability with $$D_0=H(\sigma\mid\mu_s)<\infty,\qquad F_0=\mathcal I(\sigma\mid\mu_s)<\infty,\qquad p=\mathbb E_\sigma Y,$$ then $$\label{eq:critical-translation-gain} F_0-2\lambda D_0 \ge(s^{-2}-\lambda/s)|p|^2 -C_J\sqrt a\,(F_0+D_0).$$

Fix $J\subset(0,1/2)$ compact and $s\in J$, and put $\lambda=1/R_s$. There are a smooth positive probability $\eta$ and a smooth vector field $w$, with $0R_s^P$, take the optimizer $f$ of Lemma 10 and set $$\eta=f^2\mu_s,\qquad w=D\log f^2, \qquad I=2\lambda H(\eta\mid\mu_s).$$* 2. *If $R_s=R_s^P$, there is a centered nonconstant gap eigenfunction $\varphi$ satisfying $A_{\mu_s}\varphi=\lambda\varphi$. Take $$\eta=\mu_s,\qquad w=D\varphi, \qquad I=\lambda\mathbb E_{\mu_s}\varphi^2.$$* *In either alternative, $$\label{eq:critical-uniform-smallness} |\mathbb E_\eta w|^2+\mathbb E_\eta|K_sw|^2\le C_J\sqrt a\,I, \qquad \mathbb E_\eta\langle w,K_sw\rangle\le\lambda|\mathbb E_\eta w|^2.$$ In alternative (ii) the factor $\sqrt a$ can be replaced by $a^2$. Coordinates belong to $\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}(A_\eta)$ in both alternatives.

If Theorem 1 fails, there is a sequence of dimensions and centered compactly supported log-concave laws $\mu$ satisfying Equation [eq:critical-normalization]. Fix $s=1/8$, form $\mu_s,b_s,M_s,K_s$ as in Equation [eq:critical-posterior], and put $\lambda=R_s^{-1}$. After passage to a subsequence there are smooth positive probabilities $\eta$ and smooth vector fields $w$ such that, with $A=A_\eta$ and $I=\mathbb E_\eta|w|^2$, $$\begin{gathered} \lambda\longrightarrow1,\qquad R(\eta)\le\lambda^{-1}, \qquad 0R_s^P$, $\eta=f^2\mu_s$ for the positive unit-norm optimizer, $w=D\log f^2$, and $I=2\lambda H(\eta\mid\mu_s)$. The exact deficit identity in Equation [eq:critical-exact-deficit] holds for compact square-root tests relative to $\eta$, and $A Y=(Y-b_s)/s-w$.* 2. *$R_s=R_s^P$, $\eta=\mu_s$, $A\varphi=\lambda\varphi$, $\mathbb E_\eta\varphi=0$, $w=D\varphi$, and $I=\lambda\mathbb E_\eta\varphi^2$. One may rescale $\varphi$ so that $I\to0$.* *All $o$-terms refer to the counterexample sequence with fixed finite parameters. In particular no relation between dimension, $I$, and the rate of convergence is asserted or needed here.

In the strict case, let $Y_0\sim\eta$ and let $G'$ be an independent standard Gaussian vector in the same Euclidean space. For $T\ge0$ define $$L_T=\sqrt T\,w(Y_0)+G',\qquad
 d(T)=H(\mathop{\mathrm{Law}}(L_T)\mid\gamma),$$ where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian measure. For every finite $M$, $$\sup_{0\le T\le M}d(T)=o(I).
 \label{eq:efficient-probes}$$

Let $p$ and $q$ be smooth strictly positive probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$, with $q$ log-concave. Suppose $$H_0=H(p\mid q)<\infty,\qquad
 w=D\log(p/q),\qquad I=\mathbb E_p|w|^2<\infty,
 \qquad \mathbb E_p e^{c|Y|^2}<\infty$$ for some $c>0$, where $Y\sim p$. Let $G$ be a standard Gaussian vector independent of $Y$. For $r>0$, let $U_r=Y+\sqrt rG$, let $p_r$ and $q_r$ be the Gaussian convolutions of $p$ and $q$, and put $\bar w_r(U_r)=\mathbb E_p[w(Y)\mid U_r]$ and $H_r=H(p_r\mid q_r)$. Then, for every $z>0$, $$2(H_0-H_z)\le\int_0^z\mathbb E_p|\bar w_r(U_r)|^2\,dr.
 \label{eq:prediction-entropy-loss}$$

Use the critical sequence and notation of Proposition 18, with $I\to0$ in the gap case. The following assertions hold.* 1. *For every fixed $c<\infty$, uniformly over deterministic orthogonal projections $\Pi$ with $\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}\Pi\le cI$, $$\mathbb E|\Pi w|^2=o(I). \label{eq:prediction-small-subspaces}$$* 2. *For every $\epsilon>0$, for all sufficiently far members of the sequence there is a deterministic subspace $V_\epsilon$ of dimension at most $C_\epsilon I$ such that, for every $v\perp V_\epsilon$, $$v^*(\mathbb Eww^*)v\le\epsilon|v|^2,\qquad v^*(\mathbb Eb_sb_s^*)v\le\epsilon|v|^2,\qquad v^*(\mathbb EM_s)v\le\epsilon|v|^2. \label{eq:prediction-outlier-subspaces}$$ In the gap case $V_\epsilon$ may be taken to be zero, and $\|\mathbb Eb_sb_s^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\mathbb EM_s\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1)$.* 3. *In the strict case, for every fixed $r\in(0,1/4)$ and $\epsilon>0$, the conditional covariance $C_r=\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(w(Y_0)\mid U_r)$ satisfies $$\mathbb E\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\bigl(C_r\mathbf 1_{\{C_r>\epsilon\mathrm{Id}\}}\bigr)=o(I). \label{eq:conditional-tail}$$ The indicator denotes the spectral projection. No assertion about additional Gaussian probes or Equation [eq:conditional-tail] is needed for the gap case.

Under the hypotheses of Proposition 20, there exist totally symmetric fields $T_l$ satisfying Equations [eq:hierarchy-eigen] and [eq:hierarchy-projection], with the stated operator domains. Moreover $|\mathbb ET_l|=o(\sqrt I)$ for every fixed $l$.

In the strict branch of Proposition 20, $Q=Dw$ and the fields $T_l$ constructed in Lemma 23 satisfy the following property. For every fixed $\delta>0$, each one-slot flattening $F$ of $T_l$, $l\ge1$, and also $F=Q$, obeys $$\label{eq:hierarchy-operator-tail} \mathbb E\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\bigl(FF^*\mathbf 1_{\{FF^*>\delta^2\}}\bigr)=o(I).$$ Equivalently, clipping every singular value at any fixed positive cutoff changes the field by $o(\sqrt I)$ in $L^2$.

The field $R$ belongs to the Dirichlet form domain and satisfies $$\|\mathbb ER\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=o(1),\qquad
 \liminf\|DR\|_2^2\ge1,\qquad \|DR\|_2^2=O(1).$$

There is an absolute constant $C_0$ such that, for every fixed $t>0$ and $L\ge1$, the observations in Equation [eq:obs-covariance-definition] satisfy $$\label{eq:obs-information-upper} \limsup\int_0^\infty\mathsf I(Y_t;Z_T)\,\frac{dT}{T^2}\le C_0.$$ In particular, one may take $C_0=9/4$.

In the notation of Lemma 39, put $\widetilde B_{\beta,x} =H_\beta[(\widetilde Z_{x/\beta^2})_\beta]$. For every fixed polynomial in $u,x,A_\beta,A_{u,\beta},B_{\beta,x}$ and their adjoints, its weighted trace integral over $\mathcal J\times\mathcal X$ changes by $o(1)$ if $B_{\beta,x}$ is replaced by $\widetilde B_{\beta,x}$.

Let $
u$ be a finite positive measure on $\mathbb R^k$ with $\int e^{a|w|}\,d
u(w)<\infty$ for every $a>0$. Polynomials are dense in $L^p(
u)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.

Let $n,g',g$ be independent scalar standard Gaussians and let $n_u=\alpha n+\sqrt{1-\alpha^2}\,g'$. For every fixed mixed polynomial, the weighted trace moments of $$\big(A_\beta,A_{u,\beta},\widetilde B_{\beta,x}\big)$$ converge to the corresponding scalar moments of $$\big(n,n_u,g_x(n)g\big).$$ The assertion holds after integration over compact positive $u,x$ intervals against $\kappa(u)\,du\,dx/x^2$, and permits fixed polynomial dependence on $u,x$. Adjoints in a matrix word become the identical real scalar factors in its limit.
